To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the acquisition of wh-questions is a functionally motivated process, that it is influenced by the interactional style of the child and caregiver, and that it is constrained by cognitive factors that are universal to all human languages and all human children.
children acquiring Korean, as well as other languages, first acquire wh-forms that are used for the purpose of requesting information and that are relatively simple in form.

the order in which Korean wh-forms are acquired in production and comprehension is consistent with the acquisition order of wh-forms cross-linguistically and that the acquisition order of Korean wh-forms is consistent with the order in which they are introduced into mothers' input to children.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between form and function, and the role of the child's cognitive development in the acquisition of wh-questions.
the interplay of form and function in acquisition and with the role of input and individual differences in the acquisition process.
the interrelationship of cognitive and functional constraints on language acquisition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the acquisition order of wh-questions is determined by both universal and language specific factors.
the acquisition order of wh-questions in Korean is a function of the interaction between the child's cognitive development and the child's input.
the acquisition of wh-questions is not only a function of the child's cognitive development but also of the input he/she receives.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the acquisition of wh-questions is not simply a matter of the order of acquisition of the wh-forms, as is commonly thought, but also involves a consideration of the order in which the functions of wh-forms are acquired.

children's acquisition of wh-questions follows the same general order across languages, and that the order of acquisition of particular forms in Korean follows that found in English and other languages, but that there are also some differences.
acquisition of wh-questions is a complex process involving the interplay of cognitive development, functionally based similarities and differences in input, and interactive style.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, although there are some similarities in the acquisition of wh-forms across languages and individuals, there is also a great deal of variability.
acquisition order is not only a function of the input, as has been argued by the usage-based approach, but also constrained by cognitive development, as argued by the nativist approach.
acquisition orders can be explained by both cognitive constraints on the development of wh-constructions and functional constraints on the input.
